extra.motion:
Locked-off camera, the exact same frame held for eight seconds, and it stays dark the whole time: the floodlights and stage lights stay off from start to end. Inside the darkness everything is restless: the dark outlines of heads in the near row shuffle and bob, a few arms rise as silhouettes, and the faint haze drifts slowly across the small green point on the far stage. The tiny green screen flickers slightly, like an old tube warming up. Sound: a low rumbling crowd building, whistles, stamping feet on the stands, no voices picked out, no music.
Thanks.

Handheld from inside the crowd, jostled and bumped the whole time, the same framing held. It stays dark from start to end: only the one spotlight on the man stays on, the floodlights stay off. The black silhouettes of heads and arms in the foreground sway and bob and rise, crossing the pool of light. The man on stage keeps his arms up and rocks his shoulders, slow and heavy. Haze drifts through the single beam. Sound: a crowd chanting and stamping in the dark, rising, no voices picked out, no music.
Thanks.

Handheld camera close on the head, with a short hard jolt at the start as if the operator flinched, then it pushes in slowly and keeps drifting the whole eight seconds. The word on the screen holds steady, front-on and unchanged. The head snaps up and jerks to the side, then bobs hard to a heavy beat, the cables swinging with each nod. The haze behind rolls through the green light. The rest of the frame stays black. Sound: the crackling thump of an old television switching on, then a deep electrical hum, a crowd roaring far off in the dark, no voices picked out, no music.
Thanks.

Camera on the stand looking up, with a fast short tilt up toward the bank in the first second, then it shakes slightly as if a heavy bass hit is rattling the stand, all through the clip. The rows of lamps come on row by row with hard snaps, one row per beat, until the whole bank is blazing white. Beams cut through the haze and the haze swirls in them. Sound: heavy electrical clunks of contactors switching, one per row, a building crowd roar below, no voices picked out, no music.
Thanks.

Handheld from inside the crowd, the camera jostled and bumped the whole time, pushing forward a few steps then knocked sideways. The man on stage pumps both fists up on every beat, leans into the DJ table, throws one arm out over the crowd. The foreground heads bounce up and down, arms punch the air and block part of the frame then drop away, a drink splashes up. The stage beams sweep fast left and right through the haze. Sound: a deafening crowd roar and chanting with no words picked out, no music.
Thanks.

Locked-off camera on the gantry, the frame holds still the whole time. The whole crowd erupts and keeps going for the full eight seconds: arms pumping, people jumping in waves that ripple across the stands, scarves twirled overhead, drinks thrown up in arcs, people on shoulders bouncing. The stage beams sweep side to side through the haze in fast swings, crossing and uncrossing. The man on the stage keeps his arms up and rocks his body to a heavy beat. The floodlights stay full and steady. Sound: a huge roaring crowd and the hum of the stadium, no voices picked out, no music.
Thanks.

Handheld camera along the barrier, tracking sideways fast down the front row and bouncing the whole time. The crowd surges against the barrier, people jump and slam down, arms punch the air on every beat, someone climbs up onto the barrier and is pulled back, beer flies up in a sheet and catches the white light. Faces stay mid-scream and grinning. Sound: crushing crowd roar, shouting with no words picked out, a steel barrier rattling, no music.
Thanks.

Handheld, camera bouncing with the crowd, as if the operator is jumping with them. The whole group jumps up and down together on every beat, arms locked, the stand shaking under them. Scarves whirl, beer sprays up and rains down, a man is pulled into a hug, a woman throws her head back laughing and screaming. People further up the stand jump in waves behind. Sound: a stand full of people bouncing, stamping and roaring, seats banging, no voices picked out, no music.
Thanks.

Camera close behind his shoulder, slowly pushing forward and arcing round him to the right the whole eight seconds, the crowd sliding across the background. He slowly raises one arm out toward the stadium and holds it, his head nodding hard on the beat. The crowd beyond surges and jumps in waves, arms rising together, the stage beams sweeping over them through the haze. The floodlights stay full. Sound: an enormous stadium crowd roaring, no voices picked out, no music.
Thanks.

The camera stays put at chest height, a slight handheld drift. Tarquin keeps walking forward from the left at a slow, heavy pace, splashing through a shallow puddle, then slows and stops a few bays short of the barrel. Bob takes his hand away from the fire, turns his whole body to face Tarquin and straightens up. Rain falls steadily and ripples the puddles; the flames in the drum lick and lean in the wind; the flap of one tent shakes. Sound: steady rain on tarmac and tent nylon, the crackle of the fire, a car passing on a distant road, footsteps in water. No speech.
Thanks.

Handheld camera, close and moving with the men, as if the operator is a third person in the argument. Man A on the left raps hard into Man B's face: his head bobs and juts on every beat, his bottle hand stabs toward Man B's chest three times, short and sharp, close to his own body, the beer slopping in the bottle. His feet stay planted on the tarmac; he leans in further with each jab. Man B rocks back half a step on the second jab, chin tucked, eyes locked on Man A, the flute held low and tilting, a little champagne spilling over the rim. The camera drifts a few inches left to right with Man A's lean. Rain falls through the frame, the barrel fire flickers and spits, drops pock the puddles. Mouths move but there is no speech: sound is rain on tarmac, fire crackle and distant road hum only.
Thanks.

Handheld camera, tight and moving with them, drifting a little towards whoever leans in. Bob jabs his finger at Tarquin three times in a rhythm, stepping half a pace forward on the last jab; his jaw works as he shouts. Tarquin gives ground, one half-step back, his raised hands opening palms out, then he plants his feet and stops retreating. Rain keeps falling and drips off the end of Bob's pointing hand; firelight flickers across both of them. Sound: rain, the fire, a shoe scuffing wet tarmac, breathing. No spoken words.
Thanks.

Handheld over-the-shoulder, slowly pushing in toward Man B through the whole 8 seconds. Man B raps back hard: he hunches, then snaps upright, his head bobbing on the beat; the flute hand stabs toward Man A on the stressed words, twice, the champagne sloshing up the glass; his other hand sweeps across his own chest and out. His feet stay planted. In the foreground Man A's shoulder shifts back a few inches, his head tilting as he takes it. Rain streaks through the lamp light, the barrel fire flickers on Man B's side. Mouths move, no speech: sound is rain, fire crackle and a distant car passing on wet road.
Thanks.

Start from the still. Only the man on the right of the reference is in shot. He keeps the bottle tipped up and swallows twice, his throat working, then drops it from his mouth, wipes his lips with the back of his wrist and stares off across the car park, breathing hard, shoulders rising and falling. Rain keeps falling the whole time and runs off his hair and the bottle. The fire in the drum behind him flickers and its orange light shifts on the wet tarmac. The camera is handheld and drifts slowly in towards him. Sound: rain on tarmac and on tent fabric, the crackle of the fire, a car passing on a distant road. No speech, no music. Thanks.

Start from the still. Only the man on the right of the reference is in shot. He stays on the floor and tries to push himself up on one elbow, gets halfway, his face tightening, then sinks back down onto his side and presses his hand harder into his lower back, breathing in short sharp breaths through his teeth. Cement dust drifts slowly through the shaft of daylight and settles. The camera stays low and locked off at floor level. Sound: his ragged breathing, the scrape of his shoe on concrete, a forklift reversing beep somewhere far off in the building, wind at the open roller door. No speech, no music. Thanks.

Fixed low camera with a slight handheld sway. Both men rap to the lens in step: their heads bob on the same beat, both jut forward on the same word, and their free hands chop down together, then sweep out to the side together, close to their bodies. Their drinks rise and fall with the movement, beer and champagne slopping. Feet planted in the puddle, shoes splashing a little as they bounce on their knees. Behind them the barrel fire sends sparks up into the rain. Mouths move, no speech: sound is rain, fire, and the slap of feet in water.
Thanks.

Start from the still. The screens move on their own and very fast: the columns of figures scroll in rapid bursts, charts redraw, windows open and close faster than a person could click, a mouse cursor flicks across one screen in jerky darts. On one desk a keyboard sits untouched while its screen keeps working. The coloured light from the screens flickers across the empty chairs and the paper cup. Nobody enters. The camera tracks slowly along the row at desk height, past the empty chairs. Sound: the hum of the computers, the air conditioning, a soft repeated electronic chime from one terminal. No speech, no music. Thanks.

Start from the still. The barrier arm gives a short mechanical shudder as if it is about to rise, lifts a few centimetres, then stops and drops back down with a clunk. The small lamp on the post stays solid red. Rain keeps hammering the arm and dripping off its end; the red reflection on the tarmac breaks up in the ripples. The car does not move. The camera stays locked off at window height. Sound: rain drumming on the car roof and the bonnet, the whirr and clunk of the barrier motor, the car engine idling. No speech, no music. Thanks.

Handheld over Bob's shoulder, a slow push in towards Tarquin over the 8 seconds. Tarquin swings his arm from the tents across to the supermarket front, the hand opening and closing as he points, then brings it back and slaps it once against his own chest. His head juts forward on each beat of shouting. Bob's shoulder in the foreground shifts as he holds his ground. Rain keeps coming down, flames shake the light on Tarquin's face. Sound: rain, the fire, the slap of a wet hand on a jacket, a distant shop shutter rattling in the wind. No speech.
Thanks.

Handheld camera circles a quarter turn around him, left to right, keeping him in medium shot. He keeps rapping: head bobbing and jutting, the flute hand sweeping in a slow arc across the tents and the barrel as though showing off a view, then jabbing back toward the left edge of frame on the beat, where the other man stands out of shot. His shoulders shrug in a short sneer. Feet planted, weight rocking heel to toe. Rain runs off the flute's rim. The barrel fire flickers and a tent flap shifts in the wind. Mouths move, no speech: sound is rain on tents, fire crackle, wind.
Thanks.

Start from the still. Nobody comes in. The screens carry on by themselves: the wall screen's charts redraw, a window slides open and closes, the call grid flickers between empty tiles. One leather chair, still turning slowly from when it was left, comes to rest. The light outside fades a little darker over the eight seconds and a few more windows light up across the city. The camera pushes slowly along the length of the table towards the far screen. Sound: the hum of the building's air handling, a faint electronic notification tone from the table screen, distant city traffic through the glass. No speech, no music. Thanks.

Handheld, close, the camera jolting slightly with his movements. He raps hard at the man at the right edge of frame: his head snaps forward on each stressed word, the pointing hand stabs at him three times, then twists into a flat chopping hand cutting the air between them. The bottle stays clamped to his chest, beer slopping. His shoulders rise and drop with his breath, feet planted. The dark shoulder at the right edge shifts back slightly. Rain streaks across the firelight behind. Mouths move, no speech: sound is rain and fire crackle only.
Thanks.

Start from the still. Down the aisle the robots slide across the floor in quick, exact straight lines, turn on the spot and carry their pods away; the picking arm swings, grabs a box and drops it into a tote again and again, faster than a person could. The empty vests on the hooks stay still; a draught from under the fire door stirs the fallen one on the floor slightly. No people appear. The camera holds on the vests, then racks focus to the busy aisle behind them. Sound: the electric whine of the robots, the hiss and click of the arm, boxes thudding into totes, a ventilation fan. No speech, no music. Thanks.

Start from the still. The rain hammers down the whole time, drops smacking the water and the banknote. The running water in the gutter pushes the note slowly along the kerb until it catches on the bars of the drain grate, folds over on itself and starts to be sucked down between the bars, one corner going under. A car passes in the background and its wheels throw a spray of water across the frame. The camera stays locked off at road level. Sound: heavy rain on tarmac, water gurgling into the drain, the tyre hiss of the passing car. No speech, no music. Thanks.

The camera holds close and handheld, almost motionless, a slight breathing sway. Tarquin's chest stops heaving; his jaw unclenches and his lips close. His brow lifts and relaxes, his eyes go off Bob and drop to the wet ground between them, and his head tilts down by degrees. He swallows. His shoulders sink a little. Rain keeps running down his face; the firelight flickers across his cheek. Sound: rain, the fire, his breath going out. No spoken words.
Thanks.

Slow handheld push-in toward him across 8 seconds, from medium to medium close-up. He raps quietly, small movements now: his head gives slow, small nods on the beat, his gaze stays down on the tarmac, then lifts once toward the left edge of frame and drops again. His free hand opens and closes at his side. The flute swings slightly from his fingers and one drop of champagne falls into a puddle. His weight shifts from one foot to the other. Rain keeps falling around him, puddles rippling. Mouths move, no speech: sound is rain and a far-off fire crackle.
Thanks.

Gentle handheld, nearly locked, a slight drift toward him. He raps more slowly now: his head gives three slow nods toward the man off-frame right, as if conceding a point; the hand on his chest presses flat, then lifts an inch and returns; on the last beat he raises the beer bottle a few inches from his hip toward frame right, an offer. His feet stay planted, his shoulders loosen. Rain falls between him and the camera, the barrel fire flickers behind. Mouths move, no speech: sound is rain and fire crackle only.
Thanks.

Handheld close-up, the camera nearly motionless. Bob holds the hard stare for a moment, then his jaw unlocks, his shoulders drop and he lets out a long breath that steams in the cold air. The narrowed eyes open a little; his brow lifts; he looks Tarquin up and down, then back to his face, slowly, as if seeing him properly. A small shake of the head, lips closed. Rain keeps falling; firelight moves across his face. Sound: rain, the fire crackling, one long exhale. No speech.
Thanks.

Camera holds at waist height with a slight handheld drift, then eases in a little. Tarquin closes his fingers round the lower half of the can and takes it; Bob lets go and draws his hand back. Tarquin looks up at Bob and gives one small nod. Bob nods back, then both men turn to face the fire and hold their hands out over it, standing side by side at the same height. Tarquin turns the can over in his hand. Rain falls through the heat above the drum and sparks rise. Sound: rain, the fire crackling, the tick of rain on the can. No speech.
Thanks.

Locked-off close insert, slow motion. The bottle and the flute move toward each other the last two centimetres and meet: the rim of the champagne flute knocks against the shoulder of the beer bottle in the centre of frame. On contact, the champagne rocks up one side of the flute and a few drops flick off the rim, beer foams up the neck of the bottle, raindrops on the glass shake loose. Both hands keep their grip, fingers unchanged, the glass and the bottle stay separate solid objects. Then both drinks lift together a few inches up and out of the top of frame. Rain falls through the firelight behind. Sound: one clear chink of glass on glass, then rain and fire crackle. No speech.
Thanks.

Handheld low camera, a slow push in toward both men over 8 seconds. Locked together by the arms round each other's shoulders, they shout at the lens in unison, heads jutting forward on the same beat, their raised drinks pumping up toward the rain twice together, beer and champagne spilling over their raised hands and falling with the rain. They rock side to side together as one unit, feet planted in the puddle. On the last beat both stop moving at once, drinks held high, staring straight into the lens, rain pouring, the fire behind them crackling. Mouths move, no speech: sound is heavy rain and the fire, then rain alone.
Thanks.

Locked-off camera, the exact same frame held for eight seconds, and it stays dark the whole time: floodlights and stage lights stay off from start to end. The man on the stage keeps facing the crowd and the camera the whole time, his head never turning away: he nods his head slowly and heavily on a slow beat, his shoulders rolling, one hand working the deck, the other rising slowly to point out over the crowd. His screen holds the word BADCODE steady from start to end, the same green, no flicker, no change of picture. The silhouetted crowd sways and bobs, arms rise one by one as black shapes against the green, the haze drifts slowly across the stage light. Sound: a low rumbling crowd building, stamping feet on the stands, a deep hum, no voices picked out, no music.
Thanks.
